To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
3-quinolinic acids are a new class of inhibitors of CK2, which can be used for the development of new anticancer agents.
3-quinolines were found to be a new class of inhibitors of protein kinase.
the derivatives of 2- and 3-quinolines with a carboxylic function were synthesized as new inhibitors of CK2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of new inhibitors of protein CK2.
the design and synthesis of new inhibitors of protein kinases.
the design and synthesis of new CK2 inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
3-quinolines carboxylic derivatives are a promising starting point for the development of new and selective inhibitors of CK2.
the 3-quinolinylcarboxylic acids are promising lead compounds for development of new inhibitors of CK2.
the 3-quinolinic acid derivatives with a tetrazole moiety are the most active inhibitors of the protein kinase CK2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have synthesized and identified a series of novel inhibitors for CK2.
the 2-amino-3-quinoline- carboxylic derivative 4a was the most potent inhibitor (IC50 = 0.65 μM) of CK2.
the 3-quinolines are a promising new class of protein kinase CK1α/CK2α inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a tetrazolo ring in the 4-position of quinoline-3-carbonyl group is essential for high CK2 inhibitory activity.
a combination of 2-amino-3-quinoline-carboxylic acids with tetrazole moiety is a good strategy for the design of new inhibitors of CK2.
the introduction of an additional nitrogen atom into the quinoline ring system and the presence of a carboxylate group in position 3 of the quinoline nucleus are essential for the inhibition of CK2.
